sa: यत् खलु साधु तत् सामेत्य् आचक्षते ।
iast: yat khalu sādhu tat sāmety ācakṣate ।
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
the act of sitting or being near or at hand
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Om. Surely, the meditation on the whole Saman is good. Anything that is good, people call as Saman, anything that is not good, as Asaman.

sa: साम्नैनम् उपागाद् इति साधुनैनम् उपागाद् इत्य् एव तद् आहुः ।
असाम्नैनम् उपागाद् इत्य् असाधुनैनम् उपगाद् इत्य् एव तद् आहुः ॥
iast: sāmnainam upāgād iti sādhunainam upāgād ity eva tad āhuḥ ।
asāmnainam upāgād ity asādhunainam upagād ity eva tad āhuḥ ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Thus, when people say, ‘He approached him with Saman’, then they say only this: ‘He approached him with a good motive’. And when they say, ‘He approached him with Asaman’, then they say only this" ‘He approached him with an evil motive.’

sa: साम नो बतेति यत् साधु भवति साधु बतेत्य् एव तद् आहुः ।
असाम नो बतेति यद् असाधु भवत्य् असाधु बतेत्य् एव तद् आहुः ॥
iast: sāma no bateti yat sādhu bhavati sādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ ।
asāma no bateti yad asādhu bhavaty asādhu batety eva tad āhuḥ ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret
an interjection expressing astonishment or regret

tr.text: Again, people say: ‘Oh, this is Saman for us’, when it is something good; then they say only this: ‘Oh, this is good for us’. Again, they say, ‘Oh, this is Asaman for us’, when it is not good; then they say only this: ‘Oh, this is evil.’

sa: स य एतद् एवं विद्वान् साधु सामेत्य् उपास्ते ऽभ्याशो ह यद् एनं साधवो धर्मा आ च गच्छेयुर् उप च नमेयुः ॥
iast: sa ya etad evaṃ vidvān sādhu sāmety upāste ’bhyāśo ha yad enaṃ sādhavo dharmā ā ca gaccheyur upa ca nameyuḥ ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
that which is established or firm

tr.text: When one who knows it thus meditates on the Saman as good, all good qualities hasten towards him and serve him.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Among the worlds one should meditate upon the Saman as fivefold. The earth is the syllable him, the fire is Prasrava, the sky is Udgitha, the sun is Pratihara, and heaven is Nidhana. Thus this meditation pertains to the higher worlds.
Now, among the lower worlds. Heaven is the syllable him, the sun is Prastava, the sky is Udgitha the fire is Pratihara, and the earth is Nidhana.

sa: कल्पन्ते हास्मै लोका ऊर्ध्वाश् चावृत्तश् च य एतद् एवं विद्वांल् लोकेषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: kalpante hāsmai lokā ūrdhvāś cāvṛttaś ca ya etad evaṃ vidvāṃl lokeṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: to be well ordered or regulated
to turn or draw round or back or near
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: The worlds in the ascending and descending lines belong to him. Who, knowing it thus (endowed with the quality of ‘good’) meditates on the fivefold Saman in the worlds.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as rain. The wind that precedes is the syllable him, the cloud that is formed is Prastava, the shower is Udgitha, lightning and thunder are Pratihara, and the ceasing is Nidhana. It rains for him – indeed, he causes rain – who, knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman as rain.

sa: उद्गृह्णाति तन् निधनं वर्षयति ह य एतद् एवं विद्वान् वृष्टौ पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: udgṛhṇāti tan nidhanaṃ varṣayati ha ya etad evaṃ vidvān vṛṣṭau pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: to cause to rain (Parjanya etc.) or to fall down as rain (flowers etc.)
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as rain. The wind that precedes is the syllable him, the cloud that is formed is Prastava, the shower is Udgitha, lightning and thunder are Pratihara, and the ceasing is Nidhana. It rains for him – indeed, he causes rain – who, knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman as rain.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise
a tiger (as making a lowing or roaring sound)
chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman in all the waters. When a cloud gathers, it is the syllable him. When it rains, it is Prastava. Those (waters) that flow to the east, are Udgitha. Those that flow to the west are Pratihara. The ocean is Nidhana.

sa: न हाप्सु प्रैत्य् अप्सुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् सर्वास्व् अप्सु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: na hāpsu praity apsumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān sarvāsv apsu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: possessed of or shining in the waters (e.g. the lightning which does not lose it
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who, knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman in all the waters, does not drown in water and he becomes rich in water.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as the seasons: The spring is the syllable him, the summer is Prastava, the rainy season is Udgitha, the autumn is Pratihara, and the winter is Nidhana.

sa: कल्पन्ते हास्मा ऋतव ऋतुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् ऋतुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: kalpante hāsmā ṛtava ṛtumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ṛtuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: to be well ordered or regulated
coming at regular or proper times
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He, who knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman in the seasons, him the seasons serve and he becomes rich in seasons.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the fivefold Saman as the animals. The goats are the syllable him, the sheep are Prastava, the cows are Udgitha, the horses are Pratihara, and man is Nidhana.

sa: भवन्ति हास्य पशवः पशुमान् भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् पशुषु पञ्चविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: bhavanti hāsya paśavaḥ paśumān bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān paśuṣu pañcavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: connected with or relating to cattle or animals
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He, who knowing it this, meditates on the fivefold Saman in animals, to him animals belong and he becomes rich in animals.

words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: One should meditate on the progressively higher and better fivefold Saman as the senses; The organ of smell is the syllable him, the organ of speech is Prastava, the eye is Udgitha, the ear is Pratihara, and the mind is Nidhana. Verily, these are progressively higher and better.

sa: परोवरीयो हास्य भवति परोवरीयसो ह लोकाञ् जयति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् प्राणेषु पञ्चविधं परोवरीयः सामोपास्ते ।
iast: parovarīyo hāsya bhavati parovarīyaso ha lokāñ jayati ya etad evaṃ vidvān prāṇeṣu pañcavidhaṃ parovarīyaḥ sāmopāste ।
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who knowing it thus, meditates on the fivefold Saman, progressively higher and better, in the senses, to him belong progressively higher and better lives and he wins ever higher and better worlds. So much for (the meditation on) the fivefold Saman.

sa: यत् किंच वाचो हुम् इति स हिङ्कारः ।
iast: yat kiṃca vāco hum iti sa hiṅkāraḥ ।
words: a tiger (as making a lowing or roaring sound)

tr.text: Next is the meditation on the sevenfold Saman. One should meditate on the sevenfold Saman as speech. Whatsoever in speech is ‘hum’, that is the syllable him; whatever is ‘pra’, that is Prastava; whatever is ‘a’, that is Adi (the first); whatever is ‘ut’, that is Udgitha; whatever is ‘prati’, that is Pratihara; whetever is ‘upa’, that is Upadrava; and whatever is ‘ni’, that is Nidhana.

Next is the meditation on the sevenfold Saman. One should meditate on the sevenfold Saman as speech. Whatsoever in speech is ‘hum’, that is the syllable him; whatever is ‘pra’, that is Prastava; whatever is ‘a’, that is Adi (the first); whatever is ‘ut’, that is Udgitha; whatever is ‘prati’, that is Pratihara; whetever is ‘upa’, that is Upadrava; and whatever is ‘ni’, that is Nidhana.

sa: दुग्धे ऽस्मै वाग् दोहं यो वाचो दोहः ।
य एतद् एवं विद्वान् वाचि सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: dugdhe ’smai vāg dohaṃ yo vāco dohaḥ ।
ya etad evaṃ vidvān vāci saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who knowing it thus, meditates on the sevenfold (whole) Saman as speech, for him speech yields milk i.e. its appropriate benefit, and he becomes rich in food and an eater of food.

sa: अथ खल्व् अमुम् आदित्यं सप्तविधं सामोपासीत ।
मां प्रति मां प्रतीति सर्वेण समस् तेन साम ॥
iast: atha khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta ।
māṃ prati māṃ pratīti sarveṇa samas tena sāma ॥

tr.text: Next, one should meditate upon the sevenfold Saman as the yonder sun. He is the Saman because he is always the same. He is the Saman because he is the same to all, for each one thinks, ‘He faces me, he faces me.’

sa: तस्मिन्न् इमानि सर्वाणि भूतान्य् अन्वायत्तानीति विद्यात् ।
iast: tasminn imāni sarvāṇi bhūtāny anvāyattānīti vidyāt ।
words: to low (a cow); to utter the sound hiṃ

tr.text: One should know that all these beings are dependent on him. What he is before rising, that is Himkara. On this, the animals are dependent. As they participate in the Himkara part of this Saman, do they utter him (before sunrise).

Then, the form of the sun when it has just risen, that is Prastava. On this, men are dependent. As they participate in the Prastava part of this Saman, so are they desirous of praise, direct and indirect.

sa: तस्मात् तान्य् अन्तरिक्षे ऽनारम्भणान्य् आदायात्मानं परिपतन्ति ।
words: the time when grazing cows are collected for milking or when they are together with their…
the act of taking hold of; seizing; using
to fly or run about; to wheel or whirl round; to rush to and fro

tr.text: And the form of the sun as it appears at the time of the assembling of its rays, that is Adi. On this, the birds are dependent. As they participate in the Adi part of this Saman, so do they hold themselves unsupported in the sky and fly about.

sa: अथ यत् संप्रति मध्यंदिने स उद्गीथः ।
iast: atha yat saṃprati madhyaṃdine sa udgīthaḥ ।

tr.text: Next, the form of the sun that appears just at midday, that is Udgitha. On this, the gods are dependent. As they participate in the Udgitha part of this Saman, so are they the best among the offsprings of Prajapati.

sa: अथ यद् ऊर्ध्वं मध्यंदिनात् प्राग् अपराह्णात् स प्रतिहारः ।
iast: atha yad ūrdhvaṃ madhyaṃdināt prāg aparāhṇāt sa pratihāraḥ ।
words: midday; noon; the midday offering (Savana or Pavamāna)
afternoon; the last watch of the day
to throw back; to strike or pound; to keep shut
to fall down; to glide down; to drop down

tr.text: Next, the form of the sun that appears just after midday and before (the latter part of) afternoon, that is Pratihara. On this, the foetuses are dependent. As they participate in the Pratihara part of this Saman, (so are they held up in the womb) and they do not fall down.

sa: अथ यद् ऊर्ध्वम् अपराह्णात् प्राग् अस्तम् अयात् स उपद्रवः ।
तस्मात् ते पुरुषं दृष्ट्वा कक्षं श्वभ्रम् इत्य् उपद्रवन्ति ।
iast: atha yad ūrdhvam aparāhṇāt prāg astam ayāt sa upadravaḥ ।
tasmāt te puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā kakṣaṃ śvabhram ity upadravanti ।
words: afternoon; the last watch of the day
being in or relating to a forest; forest-born; wild
to run near or towards; to run at; to rush at

tr.text: Next, the form of the sun that appears when it is past afternoon and before sunset, that is Upadrava. On this, the wild animals are dependent. As they participate in the Upadrava part of this Saman, so do they, when they see a man, run away to the forest, as to a place of safety.

sa: एवं खल्व् अमुम् आदित्यं सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: evaṃ khalv amum ādityaṃ saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste ॥

tr.text: Now, the form of the sun that appears just after sunset, that is Nidhana. On this, the fathers are dependent. As they participate in the Nidhana part of this Saman, so do people lay them aside.

sa: अथ खल्व् आत्मसंमितम् अतिमृत्यु सप्तविधं सामोपासीत ।
iast: atha khalv ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāsīta ।
words: a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: Now, verily, one should meditate on the sevenfold Saman, which has all its parts similar, and which leads beyond death. ‘Himkara, has three syllables; ‘Prastava’ has three syllables. So they are equal to each other.
‘Adi’ has two syllables; ‘Pratihara’ has four syllables. We take one syllable from Pratihara to Adi. So they are equal to each other.

sa: उद्गीथ इति त्र्यक्षरम् उपद्रव इति चतुरक्षरं त्रिभिस् त्रिभिः समं भवति ।
iast: udgītha iti tryakṣaram upadrava iti caturakṣaraṃ tribhis tribhiḥ samaṃ bhavati ।
words: chanting of the Sāmaveda (especially of the exact Sāmaveda without the additions
that which attacks or occurs suddenly

tr.text: ‘Udgitha’ has three syllables; ‘Upadrava’ has four syllables. Three and three become equal. One syllable is left over; that really is tri-syllabic; so it also becomes equal.

sa: तानि ह वा एतानि द्वाविंशतिर् अक्षराणि ॥
iast: tāni ha vā etāni dvāviṃśatir akṣarāṇi ॥

tr.text: ‘Nidhana’ has three syllables, and this to is equal (to the others). These, indeed, are the twenty two syllables (of the sevenfold Saman).

words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere

tr.text: He who, knowing this Saman thus (as good), meditates on the sevenfold Saman, which has all its parts similar and which leads beyond death, reaches the sun (Death) by the number twenty-one; for, counting from this world the yonder sun is verily the twenty-first. With the remaining twenty-second syllable he conquers the world beyond the sun. That world is of the nature of bliss, and is free from misery. (That is), he obtains victory over the sun, and then a victory still higher becomes his, who meditates on the sevenfold Saman.

sa: परो हास्यादित्यजयाज् जयो भवति य एतद् एवं विद्वान् आत्मसंमितम् अतिमृत्यु सप्तविधं सामोपास्ते सामोपास्ते ॥
iast: paro hāsyādityajayāj jayo bhavati ya etad evaṃ vidvān ātmasaṃmitam atimṛtyu saptavidhaṃ sāmopāste sāmopāste ॥
words: name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
a metrical hymn or song of praise
a metrical hymn or song of praise

tr.text: He who, knowing this Saman thus (as good), meditates on the sevenfold Saman, which has all its parts similar and which leads beyond death, reaches the sun (Death) by the number twenty-one; for, counting from this world the yonder sun is verily the twenty-first. With the remaining twenty-second syllable he conquers the world beyond the sun. That world is of the nature of bliss, and is free from misery. (That is), he obtains victory over the sun, and then a victory still higher becomes his, who meditates on the sevenfold Saman.

words: a hymn composed in the Gāyatrī metre

tr.text: The mind is Himkara, speech is Prastava, the eye is Udgitha, the ear is Pratihara, and the Prana is Nidhana. This is the Gayatra Saman woven in (the Prana and) the senses.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् गायत्रं प्राणेषु प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad gāyatraṃ prāṇeṣu protaṃ veda ।
words: a hymn composed in the Gāyatrī metre

tr.text: He who thus knows this Gayatra Saman as woven in (the Prana and) the senses, becomes the possessor of perfect senses, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should be high-minded.

One rubs, that is Himkara. The smoke is produced, that is Prastava. It blazes, that is Udgitha. The embers are formed, that is Pratihara. It goes down, that is Nidhana. It is completely extinguished, that is Nidhana. This is the Rathantara Saman woven in fire.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् रथंतरम् अग्नौ प्रोतं वेद ।
न प्रत्यङ्ङ् अग्निम् आचामेन् न निष्ठीवेत् ।
iast: sa ya evam etad rathaṃtaram agnau protaṃ veda ।
na pratyaṅṅ agnim ācāmen na niṣṭhīvet ।
words: to sip (water) from the palm of the hand for purification

tr.text: He who thus knows this Rathantara Saman as woven in fire becomes radiant with the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom, is endowed with good appetite and reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should neither sip nor spit facing the fire.

sa: प्रति स्त्रीं सह शेते स प्रतिहारः ।
iast: prati strīṃ saha śete sa pratihāraḥ ।

tr.text: The Vamadevya Saman is woven in a couple. He who thus knows this Vamadevya Saman as woven in a couple becomes one of the couple and procreates. He reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not despise any woman.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् वामदेव्यं मिथुने प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad vāmadevyaṃ mithune protaṃ veda ।
words: long; for a long time or while
to take round; to wrap round; to put aside

tr.text: The Vamadevya Saman is woven in a couple. He who thus knows this Vamadevya Saman as woven in a couple becomes one of the couple and procreates. He reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not despise any woman.

words: afternoon; the last watch of the day

tr.text: The rising sun is Himkara; the risen sun is Prastava; the midday sun is Udgitha; the sun in the afternoon is Pratihara, and the setting sun is Nidhana. This is the Brihat Saman woven in the sun.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् बृहद् आदित्ये प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad bṛhad āditye protaṃ veda ।
words: long; for a long time or while

tr.text: He who thus knows this Brihat Saman as woven in the sun becomes refulgent and endowed with good appetite, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the burning sun.

words: a tiger (as making a lowing or roaring sound)

tr.text: The white clouds gather, that is Himkara. The (rain-bearing) cloud is formed, that is Prastava. It rains, that is Udgitha. It flashes and thunders, that is Pratihara. It ceases, that is Nidhana. This is the Vairupa Saman woven in the rain-cloud.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् वैरूपं पर्जन्ये प्रोतं वेद ।
विरूपांश् च सुरूपंश् च पशून् अवरुन्धे ।
iast: sa ya evam etad vairūpaṃ parjanye protaṃ veda ।
virūpāṃś ca surūpaṃś ca paśūn avarundhe ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Virupa Saman as woven in the rain-cloud acquires cattle of handsome and manifold forms, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the rain-cloud when it rains.

words: spring; a particular metre (4 times); a particular time (in music)
winter; the cold season (comprising the two months agrahāyaṇa and Pauṣa)

tr.text: The spring is Himkara, the summer is Prastava, the rainy season is Udgitha, the autumn is Pratihara, and the winter is Nidhana. This is the Vairaja Saman woven in the seasons.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् वैराजम् ऋतुषु प्रोतं वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etad vairājam ṛtuṣu protaṃ veda ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Vairaja Saman as woven in the seasons shines with offspring, cattle and the holy effulgence born of sacred wisdom, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the seasons.
The earth is Himkara, the sky is Prastava, heaven is Udgitha, the quarters are Pratihara, and the ocean is Nidhana. This is the Sakvari Saman woven in the worlds.

sa: स य एवम् एताः शक्वर्यो लोकेषु प्रोता वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etāḥ śakvaryo lokeṣu protā veda ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Sakvari Saman woven in the worlds, becomes the possessor of the worlds, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the worlds.

words: a sheep; a woollen Soma strainer; a menstruating woman (?)

tr.text: The goats are Himkara, the sheep are Prastava, the cows are Udgitha, the horses are Pratihara, and man is Nidhana. This is the Revati Saman woven in the animals.

sa: स य एवम् एता रेवत्यः पशुषु प्रोता वेद ।
iast: sa ya evam etā revatyaḥ paśuṣu protā veda ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Revati Saman woven in the animals, becomes the possessor of animals, reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle, great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not find fault with animals.

tr.text: The hair is Himkara, the skin is Prastava, the flesh is Udgitha, the bone is Pratihara, and the marrow is Nidhana. This is the Yajnayajniya Saman woven in the limbs of the body.

sa: स य एवम् एतद् यज्ञायज्ञीयम् अङ्गेषु प्रोतं वेद ।

tr.text: He who thus knows this Yajnayajniya Saman, woven in the limbs of the body, is endowed with all the limbs, and is not crippled in any limb; he reaches the full length of life, lives gloriously, becomes great with offspring and cattle and great also with fame. His holy vow is that he should not eat fish and meat for a year, or rather, he should not eat fish and meat at all.
Fire is Himkara, Air is Prastava, the Sun is Udgitha, the Stars are Pratihara, and the Moon is Nidhana. This is the Rajana Saman woven in the deities.

His holy vow is that he should not find fault with the Brahmanas.

tr.text: The three Vedas are Himkara; the three worlds are Prastava; Fire, Air and the Sun are Udgitha; the Stars, the birds and the rays are Pratihara; the serpents, the celestial singers and the fathers are Nidhana. This is the collection of Samans woven in all things.

tr.text: Verily, he who thus knows this collection of Samans as woven in all things becomes the lord of all things.

tr.text: There is this verse about it: That which is fivefold in groups of three – there is nothing else greater or other than these (fifteen).

tr.text: He who knows that knows all. All the quarters bring offerings to him. His holy vow is that he should meditate ‘I am all’ – yea, that is his vow.

tr.text: ‘Of the Samans, I choose the one that bellows, as it were, and is good for cattle,’ thus (some think). This is the loud singing sacred to Agni, the undefined one to Prajapati, the defined one to Soma, the soft and smooth to Vayu, the smooth and strong to Indra, the heron-like to Brihaspati, and the illsounding to Varuna. Verily, one may practise all these, but should avoid the one sacred to Varuna.

tr.text: All vowels should be pronounced sonant and strong, (with the thought), ‘May I impart strength to Indra (Prana)’. All sibilants should be pronounced, neither inarticulately, nor leaving out the elements of sound, but distinctly (with the thought), ‘May I give myself to Prajapati (Virat).’ All Sparsa consonants should be pronounced slowly, without mixing them with any other letter, (with the thought), ‘May I withdraw myself from Death.’

tr.text: Three are the branches of religious duty. Sacrifice, study and gifts – these are the first. Austerity alone is the second, and the celibate student of sacred knowledge, who lives in the house of the teacher throughout his life mortifying his body in the teacher’s house, is the third. All these become possessors of meritorious worlds; but he who is established firmly in Brahman, attains immortality.

sa: तस्या अभितप्ताया एतान्य् अक्षराणि संप्रस्र्वन्त भूर् भुवः स्वर् इति ॥

tr.text: Prajapati brooded on the worlds. From them, thus brooded upon, issued forth the threefold Veda (as their essence). He brooded on this. From this, thus brooded upon, issued forth the syllables Bhuh, Bhuvah and Svah.

tr.text: He brooded on them. From them, thus brooded upon, issued forth (as their essence) the syllable Om (Brahman). Just as all the parts of the leaf, are permeated by the ribs of the leaf, so are all the words permeated by the syllable Om. Verily, the syllable Om is all this – yea, the syllable Om is verily all this.

tr.text: The expounders of Brahman say, ‘The morning libation is of the Vasus, the midday libation is of the Rudras and the third libation is of the Adityas and of the Visvadevas. Where, the, is the world of the sacrificer ?’ How can he who does not know this, perform (sacrifices) ? It is only after knowing this that he should perform (sacrifices).

sa: स यस् तं न विद्यात् कथं कुर्यात् ।

tr.text: Before the commencement of the morning chant, the sacrificer sits down behind the Garhapatya fire, facing the north and sings the Saman sacred to the Vasus: ‘(O Fire), open the door of this world that we may see you for obtaining the kingdom.’

Then he offers the oblation (with the Mantra) – ‘Salutation to Fire, who dwells in the region of the earth. Obtain the region, for me the sacrificer. This region, indeed, is to be obtained by the sacrificer. At the end of the duration of this life, I, the sacrificer, am willing to come here – Svaha.’ ‘Unbar the door of the region’, saying this he gets up. (As a result) the Vasus grant him (the region connected with) the morning libation.

tr.text: Before beginning the third libation, the sacrificer sits down behind the Ahavaniya fire, facing the north, and sings the Saman sacred to the Adityas and the one sacred to the Visvadevas: ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the sovereignty of heaven’. This is the Saman sacred to the Adityas. Next is the one sacred to the Visvadevas; ‘(O Fire), open the door of the region of heaven that we may see you for obtaining the supreme sovereignty.’
